ClientResponses.Response:
Hello! I'm sorry to hear that you did not receive a response from our Support team. We are following up with you via email now. 

It sounds like your lid has a buildup of carbonized grease. It's very common to see a substance on the inside of your grill lid that looks like peeling or flaking paint. However, we don't apply any paint or finish to the inside of our grill lids that can peel in the manner you described.
As you use your grill, vapors and grease from the grilling process can build up and create a deposit on the inside of your grill lid. The high heat of the grill will cause the the deposit to harden, and it will begin to flake or peel off. This peeling or flaking substance will be paper thin, black, and glossy on one side and matte on the other, and is known as carbonized grease.
Please clean the inside of the lid with a Weber steel bristle brush to remove the buildup. You can also use a piece of crumpled aluminum foil.
If you have any other questions, please reach out to us at Support@Weberstephen.com and we can help! Thanks!
